:::{#thm-matvec-linear}
#### A matrix maps a combination to the same combination of images

If $\matr{A}$ is an $m \times n$ matrix,
$\vecf{z}_1, \ldots, \vecf{z}_k \in \reals^n$
and $c_1, \ldots, c_k \in \reals$, then

$$
\matr{A}\,(c_1 \vecf{z}_1 + \cdots + c_k \vecf{z}_k)
= c_1\,\matr{A} \vecf{z}_1 + \cdots + c_k\,\matr{A} \vecf{z}_k.
$$

:::

::: proof

The function $\vx \mapsto \matr{A}\vx$ is a linear map
by @thm-matrix-map-linear,
and a linear map preserves linear combinations
by @thm-linear-map-lincom.
Applying that theorem with $f(\vx) = \matr{A}\vx$
and $\vecf{v}_i = \vecf{z}_i$ gives the identity.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-matvec-linear}
#### Applying a matrix to a combination

Let $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$,
$\vecf{z}_1 = (1, 0)$ and $\vecf{z}_2 = (0, 1)$.
Then $\matr{A} \vecf{z}_1 = (1, 3)$ and $\matr{A} \vecf{z}_2 = (2, 4)$,
and for the combination $2 \vecf{z}_1 - \vecf{z}_2 = (2, -1)$:

$$
\ba
\matr{A}\,(2, -1)
&= (1 \cd 2 + 2 \cd (-1),\; 3 \cd 2 + 4 \cd (-1))
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= (0, 2)
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\\
&= 2\,(1, 3) - (2, 4),
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

which is $2\,\matr{A} \vecf{z}_1 - \matr{A} \vecf{z}_2$, as @thm-matvec-linear says.

:::
